parameter: small-intestinal transit time measured by ingestible capsule in healthy volunteers (range of study values)
value: abstract: "GI transit times in the included studies ranged between 0.4 and 15.3 h for GET, 3.3-7 h for SITT, 15.9-28.9 h for CTT and 23.0-37.4 h for WGTT"
range: systematic review with narrative synthesis, no pooled estimate; 22 studies, 1885 healthy volunteers, 23 capsule systems; "GI transit times, notably GET, were influenced by the study protocol"; a capsule is an indigestible object, so its transit bounds the passage of a meal's residue, not the absorption of its nutrients; no certainty rating given; value from the abstract
citation: Nandhra GK, Chaichanavichkij P, Birch M, Scott SM 2023, J Clin Med 12:5272; doi:10.3390/jcm12165272; pmid:37629314

parameter: relation of the return of hunger after a meal to gastric emptying, blood glucose and the small-intestinal motor pattern
value: abstract: "a significant correlation between the postprandial increase in hunger ratings and the time for 90% of the meal to empty (r = 0.75, p less than 0.02)"; "hunger ratings started to increase in three subjects when over 40% of the food still remained in the stomach, and they continued to increase in all subjects even when the meal had ceased to empty from the stomach"; "The increase in hunger was not related to any consistent change in plasma glucose concentration"; the authors' reading: "the return of hunger is directly related to a decline in the exposure of the upper small intestine to nutrient stimuli, but could be modulated by gastric distension"
range: single-condition study with within-subject correlations, no control arm; the meal's size and composition are not stated in the abstract; value from the abstract

parameter: intestinal glucose absorption rate constant of the Dalla Man oral glucose absorption model (gut compartment to plasma), restated with the model's gastric constants
value: Table A.1: kabs 0.023 1/min ("Inverse of intestinal glucose absorption time constant"); kmax 0.0465 1/min and kmin 0.0076 1/min ("Maximum" and "Minimum inverse of gastric emptying time constant"); kgri 0.0465 1/min; b 0.69; c 0.17; derived: half-life of the gut compartment ln 2 / 0.023 = 30.1 min, mean residence 1 / 0.023 = 43.5 min
range: a 2023 review preprint restating the constants it simulated with and attributing the row jointly to Dalla Man et al. 2006 (IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 53:2472-2478, doi:10.1109/tbme.2006.883792) and 2007 (IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 54:1740-1749, doi:10.1109/tbme.2007.893506) without naming the table; both primaries are IEEE paywalls and were not read; the primaries fitted the model to multiple-tracer meal rate-of-appearance data
population: model constants (the primaries' healthy-adult fitting data)
citation: Ritschel TKS, Reenberg AT, Carstensen PE, Bendsen J, Jørgensen JB 2023, arXiv:2307.16444 (Mathematical meal models for simulation of human metabolism); doi:10.48550/arXiv.2307.16444; url:https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.16444

parameter: carbohydrate absorption time constant of the Hovorka meal model (two-compartment gut absorption), restated
value: Table A.1: tau_D 40 min ("Time constant"); A_G 0.8 ("Carbohydrate bioavailability")
range: a 2023 review preprint restating the constants of Hovorka et al. 2004 (Physiol Meas 25:905-920), a type 1 diabetes control model whose single tau_D lumps gastric emptying and absorption; the primary was not read
population: model constants (the primary's population not read)
citation: Ritschel TKS, Reenberg AT, Carstensen PE, Bendsen J, Jørgensen JB 2023, arXiv:2307.16444 (Mathematical meal models for simulation of human metabolism); doi:10.48550/arXiv.2307.16444; url:https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.16444

parameter: glucose entering the systemic circulation and its disposal over 6 h after a mixed meal
value: abstract: "During a 6-h postprandial period, a total of approximately 98 g of glucose were disposed of. This was more than the glucose contained in the meal ( approximately 78 g) due to persistent endogenous glucose release ( approximately 21 g): splanchnic tissues initially took up approximately 23 g, and an additional approximately 75 g were removed from the systemic circulation"
range: triple-isotope study, one meal, no control arm; the meal's energy is not stated in the abstract; value from the abstract
citation: Woerle HJ, Meyer C, Dostou JM et al 2003, Am J Physiol Endocrinol Metab 284:E716-E725; doi:10.1152/ajpendo.00365.2002; pmid:12475753

parameter: rate of appearance of glucose in plasma after a high- vs a low-glycaemic-index breakfast cereal at 50 g available carbohydrate
value: abstract: "The GI of CF was more than twice that of BC (131.5 +/- 33.0 compared with 54.5 +/- 7.2; P < 0.05), despite no significant differences in the rate of appearance of glucose into the plasma during the 180-min period"
range: two-occasion crossover over 180 min with a constant-rate [6,6-2H2]glucose infusion; the lower GI came from earlier insulin and glucose disappearance, not slower appearance; value from the abstract
citation: Schenk S, Davidson CJ, Zderic TW, Byerley LO, Coyle EF 2003, Am J Clin Nutr 78:742-748; doi:10.1093/ajcn/78.4.742; pmid:14522732

parameter: rate of appearance of exogenous glucose after pasta vs wheat bread (slowly vs rapidly digestible starch)
value: abstract: GIP concentrations after pasta were lower than after bread and "strongly correlated with the RaE (r = 0.82, P < 0.01)"; "Slower intestinal uptake of glucose from a starchy food product can result in lower postprandial insulin and GIP concentrations, but not necessarily in a lower glycemic response"
range: crossover with 13C-enriched foods and a primed-continuous D-[6,6-2H2]glucose infusion; the abstract gives the direction (slower RaE from pasta) and no RaE values or durations; value from the abstract
citation: Eelderink C, Schepers M, Preston T, Vonk RJ, Oudhuis L, Priebe MG 2012, Am J Clin Nutr 96:1017-1024; doi:10.3945/ajcn.112.041947; pmid:22990033

parameter: postprandial glucose dip at 2-3 h as a predictor of hunger and later intake
value: abstract: "the average postprandial glucose dip at 2-3 h relative to baseline level predicted an increase in hunger at 2-3 h (r = 0.16, P < 0.001), shorter time until next meal (r = -0.14, P < 0.001), greater energy intake at 3-4 h (r = 0.19, P < 0.001) and greater energy intake at 24 h (r = 0.27, P < 0.001)"
range: cohort with continuous glucose monitors: 8,624 standardized meals and 71,715 ad libitum meals in a UK exploratory and a US validation cohort; the correlations are small; value from the abstract
citation: Wyatt P, Berry SE, Finlayson G et al 2021, Nat Metab 3:523-529; doi:10.1038/s42255-021-00383-x; pmid:33846643

parameter: cumulative release of dietary-protein-derived amino acids into the circulation after 25 g vs 100 g protein (a load-dependent duration)
value: Results (Figures 6A and 6D): after 25 g protein, release "averaged 51%, 62%, and 66% over 4, 8, and 12 h, respectively"; after 100 g protein release "did not plateau, with 26%, 44%, and 53% of the ingested-protein-derived amino acids appearing over 4, 8, and 12 h, respectively"; 12-h amounts 53 ± 7 vs 16 ± 1 g; derived: 100 g released 26 g in the first 4 h, 6.5 g/h
range: randomised double-blind placebo-controlled parallel trial, n = 12 per group (0, 25 and 100 g); intrinsically labelled milk protein concentrate taken after resistance exercise; quadruple isotope tracer; release into the circulation is net of splanchnic extraction, so it understates absorption
citation: Trommelen J, van Lieshout GAA, Nyakayiru J et al 2023, Cell Rep Med 4:101324; doi:10.1016/j.xcrm.2023.101324; pmid:38118410

parameter: fraction and timing of dietary-protein-derived phenylalanine released into the circulation over 5 h after 20 g casein
value: abstract: "55.3±2.7% of the protein-derived phenylalanine was released in the circulation during the 5 h post-prandial period"; Results (Figure 5A): exogenous phenylalanine appearance rates "reached peak values at 90 min after protein ingestion (187±17 ηmol·kg -1 ·min -1"
range: single-arm study with intrinsically labelled casein and arterial and venous sampling to 300 min; the unit is printed with a Greek eta (read as nmol)
citation: Groen BB, Horstman AM, Hamer HM et al 2015, PLoS One 10:e0141582; doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0141582; pmid:26556791

parameter: time course of plasma amino acids after whey (fast) vs casein (slow) protein meals
value: abstract: "WP induced a dramatic but short increase of plasma amino acids. CAS induced a prolonged plateau of moderate hyperaminoacidemia, probably because of a slow gastric emptying"; leucine oxidation and balance followed over 7 h
range: dual-tracer study with intrinsically 13C-leucine-labelled proteins; leucine intake identical in both meals (380 micromol/kg); the abstract gives no n, protein doses or timings; value from the abstract
citation: Boirie Y, Dangin M, Gachon P, Vasson MP, Maubois JL, Beaufrère B 1997, Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A 94:14930-14935; doi:10.1073/pnas.94.26.14930; pmid:9405716

parameter: retention of dietary fat in the jejunal mucosa 5-6 h after a 50 g fat load, and its release by a later glucose drink
value: abstract: after 50 g fat at t = 0 and water or 38 g glucose at 5 h, jejunal biopsies at 6 h from those given glucose "exhibited significantly less staining for lipid within the mucosa and submucosa of the jejunum than was evident in patients that had consumed only water (p=0.028)"; glucose at 5 h "resulted in a postprandial peak in plasma TG, chylomicron-TG, and apolipoprotein B48 concentration compared with oral water"
range: two-group biopsy study plus a 5-subject metabolic subgroup; allocation method not stated in the abstract; value from the abstract
citation: Robertson MD, Parkes M, Warren BF et al 2003, Gut 52:834-839; doi:10.1136/gut.52.6.834; pmid:12740339

parameter: appetite after the same 400 kcal soup given orally, intragastrically (covert, overt) or intraduodenally at the rate of normal gastric emptying
value: abstract: "Infusion of the soup into the small intestine at a rate commensurate with normal gastric emptying exerted no significant suppression of ratings of hunger and desire to eat and no significant production of fullness"; covert intragastric infusion suppressed appetite; oral soup "produced the greatest suppression of appetite compared with other conditions" and slower gastric emptying than both intragastric infusions
range: within-subject comparison of 425 ml (400 kcal) tomato soup by route; ratings over 2 h, no intake measure; value from the abstract
citation: Cecil JE, Francis J, Read NW 1998, Appetite 31:377-390; doi:10.1006/appe.1998.0177; pmid:9920689

parameter: buffet energy intake after 120-min intraduodenal glucose at 1, 2 or 4 kcal/min vs saline (a load threshold)
value: abstract: "All glucose infusions suppressed antral (P < 0.05), but only G4 decreased duodenal, pressure waves (P < 0.01), resulted in a sustained stimulation of basal pyloric pressure (P < 0.01), and decreased energy intake (P < 0.05)"; the rises in insulin, GLP-1, GIP and CCK were related to the glucose load (r > 0.82); derived: infused energy 120, 240 and 480 kcal
range: double-blind randomised crossover; buffet immediately after the infusion; the abstract gives no intake values; value from the abstract
citation: Pilichiewicz AN, Chaikomin R, Brennan IM et al 2007, Am J Physiol Endocrinol Metab 293:E743-E753; doi:10.1152/ajpendo.00159.2007; pmid:17609258

parameter: buffet energy intake after 50-min intraduodenal lipid at 0.25, 1.5 or 4 kcal/min vs saline
value: abstract: "Only IL4 reduced energy intake (in kcal: control, 1,289 +/- 62; IL0.25, 1,282 +/- 44; IL1.5, 1,235 +/- 71; and IL4, 1,139 +/- 65 compared with control and IL0.25, P < 0.05)"; IL0.25 suppressed hunger (P < 0.05); derived: IL4 infused 200 kcal and lowered intake by 150 kcal (11.6 %) against control
range: double-blind randomised crossover, four occasions, Intralipid; +/- as given (SEM not named in the abstract); value from the abstract
citation: Pilichiewicz AN, Papadopoulos P, Brennan IM et al 2007, Am J Physiol Regul Integr Comp Physiol 293:R2170-R2178; doi:10.1152/ajpregu.00511.2007; pmid:17942490

parameter: persistence of intraduodenal lipid effects after the infusion stops, by load and duration (1.33 kcal/min for 50 or 150 min, 4 kcal/min for 50 min)
value: abstract: "The effect of the 4 kcal/min infusion was sustained so that the suppression of antral pressure waves (PWs) and PWSs and increase in PYY remained evident after cessation of the infusion (all P < 0.05)"; "There was no significant effect of any of the lipid infusions on appetite or energy intake, although nausea was slightly higher (P < 0.05) with the 4 kcal/min infusion"
range: double-blind randomised crossover, four occasions; intake measured immediately after the infusions; value from the abstract
citation: Pilichiewicz AN, Little TJ, Brennan IM et al 2006, Am J Physiol Regul Integr Comp Physiol 290:R668-R677; doi:10.1152/ajpregu.00606.2005; pmid:16210415

parameter: buffet energy intake after 60-min intraduodenal protein at 0.5, 1.5 or 3 kcal/min vs saline
value: abstract: "energy intake was reduced only after a protein load of 3 kcal/min compared with after all other treatments (P < 0.05)"; derived: infused energy 30, 90 and 180 kcal
range: randomised double-blind crossover, four occasions, 4 ml/min; buffet immediately after; the abstract gives no intake values; value from the abstract
citation: Ryan AT, Feinle-Bisset C, Kallas A et al 2012, Am J Clin Nutr 96:474-482; doi:10.3945/ajcn.112.038133; pmid:22854403

parameter: buffet energy intake after 90-min isocaloric (3 kcal/min) intraduodenal lipid, protein or lipid:protein mixtures vs control
value: abstract: "Compared with the control, L3 and P3 but not L2P1 or L1P2 suppressed EI (P < 0.05) without major effects on appetite"; "L3 but not P3 increased nausea (P < 0.05)"; derived: infused energy 270 kcal
range: randomised double-blind crossover, five occasions; the abstract gives no intake values; value from the abstract
citation: Ryan AT, Luscombe-Marsh ND, Saies AA et al 2013, Am J Clin Nutr 98:300-311; doi:10.3945/ajcn.113.061333; pmid:23803895

parameter: energy intake after 120-min intraduodenal lipid vs glucose at 2.86 kcal/min vs saline
value: abstract: "lipid infusion suppressed energy intake by 22% compared with the control infusion and by 15% compared with the glucose infusion"; "Both the lipid and glucose infusions were associated with greater fullness than the control infusion"; the suppression "was due to slower eating (P < 0.01)"; derived: infused energy 343 kcal
range: three occasions on separate days; obese and nonobese groups did not differ; value from the abstract
population: 20 healthy men aged 18-33 y (9 obese, 11 nonobese)
citation: Chapman IM, Goble EA, Wittert GA, Horowitz M 1999, Am J Clin Nutr 69:6-12; doi:10.1093/ajcn/69.1.6; pmid:9925116

parameter: food intake after 120-min intraduodenal lipid vs glucose at 2.86 kcal/min in young vs older men
value: abstract: "I.d. lipid suppressed food intake in both the young and older men (p < 0.05), whereas i.d. glucose suppressed food intake only in the older men (p < 0.05)"
range: three occasions (saline, lipid, glucose), isovolumetric; value from the abstract
population: 13 older (65-84 y) and 13 young (18-32 y) healthy men
citation: MacIntosh CG, Horowitz M, Verhagen MA et al 2001, Am J Gastroenterol 96:997-1007; doi:10.1111/j.1572-0241.2001.03684.x; pmid:11316218

parameter: food intake after 90-min intraduodenal fructose vs glucose at 2 kcal/min vs saline
value: abstract: "Intraduodenal fructose suppressed food intake compared with saline (P < 0.05) and glucose (P = 0.07)"; the GLP-1 responses to the two sugars did not differ
range: 25 % solutions at 2 ml/min; buffet at the end of the infusion; value from the abstract
citation: Rayner CK, Park HS, Wishart JM et al 2000, Am J Physiol Regul Integr Comp Physiol 278:R360-R366; doi:10.1152/ajpregu.2000.278.2.r360; pmid:10666136

parameter: hunger, CCK and energy intake with glucose delivered to the duodenum vs the mid-jejunum (1 kcal/min, 90 min)
value: abstract: "Stimulation of CCK and suppression of hunger were greater (each P<0.05), and energy intake less (P=0.05), with duodenal compared to mid-jejunal glucose infusion"; "there was minimal GLP-1 increment on either day"
range: two days in randomised order, ports 15 and 100 cm beyond the pylorus; value from the abstract
citation: Chaikomin R, Wu KL, Doran S et al 2008, Regul Pept 150:38-42; doi:10.1016/j.regpep.2008.02.006; pmid:18396340

parameter: time course of GLP-1 and GIP during intraduodenal glucose at 1 kcal/min for 120 min
value: abstract: "During intraduodenal glucose, plasma GLP-1 increased at 15 and 30 min (P<0.001 for both) and returned to baseline thereafter. In contrast, there were sustained increases in plasma GIP (P<0.001), insulin (P<0.001), and blood glucose (P<0.001)"
range: retrospective analysis of all of one laboratory's studies at this load; no appetite outcome; mean +/- SEM; value from the abstract
citation: Kuo P, Chaikomin R, Pilichiewicz A et al 2008, Regul Pept 146:1-3; doi:10.1016/j.regpep.2007.09.032; pmid:17964673

parameter: ad libitum intake after a 90-min glucose infusion (15 g) into the ileum vs the duodenum, mid-morning after breakfast
value: abstract: glucose-to-ileum "decreased ad libitum EI at lunch compared with glucose-to-duodenum [-22%, -988 ± 379 kJ (mean ± SEM), Tukey's post hoc, P < 0.05]"; "Although glucose to the duodenum also suppressed appetite ratings, eating behavior was not altered"; derived: the infusion carried 235 kJ, so lunch fell by about 4.2 times the infused energy
range: blinded randomised 4-treatment crossover with a multilumen tube; 14 randomised, 13 completed; value from the abstract
citation: Poppitt SD, Shin HS, McGill AT et al 2017, Am J Clin Nutr 106:725-735; doi:10.3945/ajcn.117.157248; pmid:28701300

parameter: ad libitum intake after a 60-min infusion of 15 g protein into the duodenum, jejunum or ileum vs placebo
value: abstract: "Intraileal protein infusion decreased ad libitum food intake compared with both intraduodenal and placebo infusion (ileum: 628.5±63 kcal vs duodenum: 733.6±50 kcal, P<0.01 and placebo: 712.2±53 kcal, P<0.05)"; "None of the treatments affected VAS scores for hunger and satiety nor plasma concentrations of PYY and glucose"
range: double-blind randomised placebo-controlled crossover after a standardised breakfast; value from the abstract
citation: van Avesaat M, Ripken D, Hendriks HF, Masclee AA, Troost FJ 2017, Int J Obes (Lond) 41:217-224; doi:10.1038/ijo.2016.196; pmid:27811949

parameter: ad libitum intake after a 90-min ileal infusion of fat, casein or sucrose (17.2 or 51.7 kcal) vs saline
value: abstract: "HL: 464.3±90.7 kcal, P<0.001; HP: 458.0±78.6 kcal, P<0.005; HC: 399.0±57.0 kcal, P<0.0001 vs control: 586.7±70.2 kcal"; "A reduction in energy intake was still apparent when the caloric amount of infused nutrients was added to the amount eaten during the ad libitum meal"; derived: 51.7 kcal of fat, casein or sucrose lowered intake by 122, 129 and 188 kcal
range: randomised single-blind crossover with a naso-ileal catheter, infusion 30 min after a standardised breakfast; value from the abstract
citation: van Avesaat M, Troost FJ, Ripken D, Hendriks HF, Masclee AA 2015, Int J Obes (Lond) 39:235-243; doi:10.1038/ijo.2014.112; pmid:24957485

parameter: satiety after 3 g or 9 g of fat perfused into the ileum (t = 105-150 min) after a fat-free liquid breakfast
value: abstract: "Ileal fat perfusion of both 3 and 9 g ... significantly increased satiety during and after fat perfusion, without differences in satiety between" the doses; "During ileal fat infusion, CCK increased dose dependently, whereas PYY concentrations increased significantly only after 9 g of fat"
range: randomised single-blind crossover with a 290-cm nasoileal tube; VAS only, no intake measure; value from the abstract
population: 16 healthy normal-weight volunteers (6 male; mean age 26 y)
citation: Maljaars PW, Symersky T, Kee BC et al 2008, Int J Obes (Lond) 32:1633-1639; doi:10.1038/ijo.2008.166; pmid:18794896

parameter: food intake and hunger during jejunal or ileal infusion of a corn-oil emulsion at 4.9 kcal/min
value: abstract: infusion into either the ileum or the jejunum "significantly reduced the period of eating (p less than 0.01) and the quantity of food consumed (p less than 0.01)"; jejunal lipid "also significantly reduced the sensations of hunger before the meal (p less than 0.05)"; "Ileal infusion did not influence these indices"
range: paired lipid vs saline studies in two groups of six; value from the abstract
population: 12 healthy non-obese male volunteers (two groups of six)
citation: Welch IM, Sepple CP, Read NW 1988, Gut 29:306-311; doi:10.1136/gut.29.3.306; pmid:3356362

parameter: food intake and gastric emptying during ileal infusion of a corn-oil emulsion vs albumen and saline
value: abstract: during ileal fat, subjects consumed "a smaller amount of food (670 +/- 23 g vs. 884 +/- 89 g) and energy (1016 +/- 79 kcal vs. 1591 +/- 228 kcal)"; ileal corn oil "delayed gastric emptying compared with ileal infusion of albumen and saline (t1/2 = 203 +/- 48 vs. 68 +/- 12 min, p less than 0.02)"; intravenous lipid did not affect intake
range: paired experiments: intake n = 6, gastric emptying n = 5, intravenous arm n = 6; value from the abstract
citation: Welch I, Saunders K, Read NW 1985, Gastroenterology 89:1293-1297; doi:10.1016/0016-5085(85)90645-6; pmid:4054521

parameter: independent gastrointestinal determinants of energy intake after intraduodenal lipid or protein (pooled analysis of nine studies)
value: abstract: "In the model including the protein studies, only BPP was identified as an independent determinant of energy intake (P < 0.05). No single parameter was identified across all models, and effects of the variables identified were relatively small"
range: pooled individual-data mixed-effects analysis of nine published studies from one laboratory; no certainty rating given; value from the abstract
citation: Schober G, Lange K, Steinert RE et al 2016, Physiol Rep 4:e12943; doi:10.14814/phy2.12943; pmid:27613824

parameter: decay half-time of hunger suppression or of a later meal's intake reduction after an intestinal nutrient infusion stops (the clearance of a gut satiety signal measured directly)
range: named by the 2026-10-12 transit harvest; the infusion studies read measure intake immediately after the infusion, and the one that followed a 4 kcal/min lipid arm past its end (Pilichiewicz 2006) reports persistent PYY and motor effects but no appetite effect; no study read varied the delay between the infusion's end and the test meal

parameter: time course of the fraction of a mixed meal's energy present in the small-intestinal lumen (unabsorbed) after ingestion
range: named by the 2026-10-12 transit harvest; the rows read give gastric emptying (S1242, S1272), capsule transit (Nandhra 2023) and appearance in plasma (Woerle 2003, Trommelen 2023, Groen 2015), never luminal nutrient mass over time
